about: The canon: every upstream this repo is allowed to build on. Repos are pinned to a commit in upstreams.lock.json by `scripts/canon resolve`. Roles: foundation (we build on it), platform (we run on it), standard (we conform to it), tool (we run it), source (we install content from it), reference (we read it, never install it blind), watch (not adopted; tracked for convergence).

upstreams.why: The agent harness itself; its docs define every config layer this repo uses. The terminal CLI is installed at this pin and held at or above it (ADR 0022). Since ADR 0065 the pin is a floor: the CLI updates itself on the latest channel, which the settings template names, so a newer release runs before it is read here: in the background in a session with no update switch (Orca sets one in each launch that submits a prompt), or at once with claude update; a move of the pin also changes minimumVersion in home/.claude/settings.json. Moved 2026-11-11 to v2.1.322 (published 2026-11-10; its only note: fast mode on Vertex in the global, us and eu regions), the version this machine already runs.
Official library form of the Claude Code harness for headless runtime workers.
Anthropic's example skills, skill template and spec; README labels them demonstration quality.
The open Agent Skills (SKILL.md) standard adopted across agent clients.
Cross-tool agent instruction file, stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation); Claude Code reads it via import.
Anthropic's plugin marketplace. Nothing is installed from it. It cannot be pinned as a whole, serves one SHA per plugin that Anthropic chooses, and auto-updates by default (ADR 0004).
Most-adopted community skills/workflow collection; listed in Anthropic's official marketplace. Read for patterns; not enabled without review.
News fragments, one file per change in a directory of its own: the pattern the handbook's practice and row files follow. Read only; not installed or run, and its collecting build step is not taken.
One Markdown file per change, named so that two never collide: the pattern the handbook's practice and row files follow. Read only; not installed or run.
Postmortem action items with an owner and a verifiable end state: the pattern behind the journal entry's owner and closes fields. Read only; nothing copied beyond short quotations.
Leading spec-driven workflow by adoption, but the field has not converged (Spec Kit vs BMAD vs Superpowers).
De facto ADR format; 4.0.0 is the current release.
Defines the Pinned-Dependencies and Dependency-Update-Tool checks this repo's pinning rule follows.
Anthropic's reference OpenTelemetry collector + Prometheus + Grafana setup for Claude Code telemetry.

Most-adopted local token/cost reporter; reads Claude Code's own session logs, no backend needed. Moved 2026-11-11 to v20.0.49 (published 2026-11-10; notes: 1h cache writes in JSON model breakdowns, a cline adapter, in-window counting in unified session reports, a codex parser guard, a faster claude report; nothing breaking). The version is in .claude/skills/lane-report/SKILL.md's npx command, mise.toml's comment and ADR 0008's table; the past run ADR 0007 records, scripts/test-land's fixture and scripts/check-addresses' example stay as written.

The OpenTelemetry Collector's core distribution (otelcol), which ships the OTLP receiver, the file exporter and the filter and transform processors (distributions/otelcol/manifest.yaml). It receives Claude Code's and Codex's OTLP log events on 127.0.0.1 only, keeps the three event types and the attributes scripts/lanes --rates reads, and writes them to ~/.claude/canon/otel/logs.jsonl with rotation. Installed by mise's github: backend (no mise or aqua registry entry exists), run as a launchd user agent by scripts/automation.

The status-line renderer, a Claude Code plugin (Node 22.18 or later; mise pins 24). home/.claude/canon/statusline.sh stays the configured command: it does canon's writes, then runs the newest installed version's hud.mjs from the marketplace user settings enable (the plugin's own launcher would run the newest copy from any marketplace) and shows its lines, with terminal hyperlinks removed and e-mail addresses, the repository owner and the home user name scrubbed; with the plugin absent or failing it shows canon's own line. Its logic runs under Node's permission model with an import fence that refuses network modules (fence.mjs, hud.mjs); git's status read runs with protocol.allow=never and every git call with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH. It writes its own data folder and, on each render, heartbeat.json with the status-line input (mode 600) under ~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/. It reads the status-line input, the transcript, ~/.claude.json's oauthAccount (shown only by showAuth/showAuthUser, both off in canon's claude-hud.json), CLAUDE.md, rules and settings. The plugin brings one skill, /hud, whose install step rewrites statusLine and is not to be run here. v0.15.0 is the newest tag; later release commits (0.15.3) are untagged.

Pinned, lockfile-backed tool versions installable without sudo. Moved 2026-11-11 to v2026.11.6 (published 2026-11-10, the newest published release; tag v2026.11.7 exists with no release and is not taken). Notes against v2026.11.5: mise run --multi, unprefixed [bootstrap.packages] keys, npm tools from HTTPS tarballs, named daemon ports, launchd resource limits, history.lock_wait; changed: the default prompt theme is now base16; fixes to TOML task usage, MISE_ORIGINAL_CWD with --cd, mise env --dotenv quoting, undefined env template errors (which no longer list every variable name) and command wrappers during installs. Nothing touches the keys mise.toml uses. The version is in scripts/bootstrap (MISE_VERSION), .github/workflows/ci.yml (the mise-action version input) and ADR 0008's table; the observations recorded under 2026.11.5 (home/.claude/canon/paper-session.sh, scripts/canon's self-test fixture, the trials of ADRs 0029, 0033, 0040, 0050 and 0069) stay as written. The machine's mise moves with mise self-update; the maintenance agent does not run it.
Python project/venv manager; the install path NautilusTrader itself recommends.

Backtest + live engine sharing one strategy codebase. v2 is the line upstream docs describe; still a release candidate. Held 2026-11-10: v2.0.0rc9 (pre-release, published 2026-11-10) lists 89 breaking changes; the five that touch names this repository uses are in ADR 0009's Evidence and are the scope for reading it against the adapter before it moves. Look again 2026-11-13.
Last stable v1 release; v1 now receives critical security backports only (branch develop_v1). Fallback if v2 stable slips.

NautilusTrader's built-in external message bus backing at the pin (docs/concepts/message_bus.md: 'Redis is the built-in external backing'; minimum 6.2). One process publishes the live mover list onto a Redis stream on 127.0.0.1 and the nodes that trade read it, so the list crosses processes without a file handoff. Installed only on request from mise's bus config environment (mise.bus.toml), which a plain install and hosted CI never read.
Alpaca's official Python SDK; the older alpaca-trade-api-python was archived on 2026-06-17.

The HTTP library alpaca-py's REST clients use; already installed as alpaca-py's dependency, now imported directly by the Alpaca adapter for a transport adapter that gives every request a default timeout, which alpaca-py does not set (ADR 0039). The version is the one uv.lock already held.
Alpaca's official MCP server (v2 is a full rewrite). Not enabled: it selects live trading from one environment variable and its default toolset includes close-all and cancel-all.

Alpaca's official SKILL.md set. The four trading skills were read at this commit and none is enabled: unpinned installs, live switches by environment variable, safeguards that are instructions only (ADR 0004).
Alpaca's official plugin marketplace for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Contents not read; not enabled.
Official Go CLI for the Trading API, labelled Alpha Preview upstream; not adopted until it leaves alpha.
Community Alpaca adapter for NautilusTrader: 0 stars, no releases, unreviewed. Reference only.
Community Alpaca adapter for NautilusTrader: 0 stars, self-described alpha, unreviewed. Reference only.
Test runner. NautilusTrader's own testing guide prescribes pytest free functions and fixtures, and pytest's docs define the tests layout this repo uses.
Python linter and formatter. NautilusTrader lints and formats with it, so adapter code matches upstream style.

Type checker. Beta upstream (0.0.x, no stable API) and the field is contested; chosen because it is the one type checker NautilusTrader runs at all, though only on its examples, and held to an exact pin.

upstreams.license: GPL-3.0 (run as a tool, not linked)
upstreams.why: Static analysis for the shell scripts and hooks, which are most of this repo's own code and run machine-wide.
Secret scanner. A trading repo handles API keys; nothing with a credential may reach a commit.
Checks GitHub Actions workflow files locally, which is the only check a workflow can get before the repo has a remote.
Checks the repo out in CI. Referenced in the workflow by commit SHA.
Installs in CI exactly the tools mise.lock records, so CI and this Mac run the same versions. Referenced in the workflow by commit SHA.
37signals' local-CI practice: run the checks on your own machine and mark the commit green with a `signoff` status. scripts/land follows the convention; the tool itself is not installed.

GitHub's own dependency update service. It reads .github/dependabot.yml and opens pull requests for the indirect packages in uv.lock and for the workflow's actions. GitHub runs it at a version this repo cannot choose, so the pin records the source that was read, not a release.

The cockpit Claude Code sessions run in: one git worktree and agent terminal per task, in one window. It starts the installed claude, so this repo's settings, hooks and instructions apply unchanged, and it reads orca.yaml for the worktree setup command. The app auto-updates by default on its stable channel, about a release a day, so this repo does not choose the version that runs; the entry follows main, and the docs it cites were read at v1.4.255. Its bundled skills orca-cli and orchestration are used within the limits of ADR 0021. It also loads a Claude Code plugin of its own, orca-agent-view, into each terminal session it starts; ADR 0023 says what that plugin does, why it stays on, and the risk it carries.

OpenAI's Codex CLI, a second agent runtime from another model family, used only as an Orca worker that reads a change and reports findings: an additional reader beside /code-review that never edits, lands or blocks (ADR 0043). Installed machine-level (mise use -g codex@<pin>, aqua:openai/codex), not in mise.toml; check with codex --version. Upstream tags about eight rust-vX.Y.Z-alpha.N pre-releases per stable release; scripts/canon outdated ignores them for this stable pin. Moved 2026-11-11 to rust-v0.167.1 (released 2026-11-10; two commits against rust-v0.167.0: opt-in incremental tools for the regular OpenAI Responses provider, and legacy incremental tools restricted to Amazon Bedrock providers; nothing under codex-rs/otel, so the event names home/.codex/otel.toml and ADR 0007 rest on are unchanged). This machine ran 0.167.0 when the pin moved; its binary moves with mise use -g codex@0.167.1 once the pin is on main.

upstreams.license: UNVERIFIED (proprietary; Meta's pages read state no licence or terms)
upstreams.why: Meta's Muse Code CLI, a review-only Orca worker from another model family (ADR 0045, under ADR 0043's terms). No public repository, so no lock pin: version 1.4.15-R8339.1, installed machine-level by the owner through mise's muse tool (requested as latest), which reads Meta's muse-stable channel, a channel that publishes only the current release, so the next mise upgrade moves it; not in mise.toml; check with muse --version. Approval and an OS sandbox are on by default, a Read-only profile exists, and --yolo turns approval and sandbox off.

upstreams.license: UNVERIFIED (no licence file in the repository; GitHub reports none)
upstreams.why: Google's Antigravity CLI (agy), a review-only Orca worker from another model family (ADR 0045, under ADR 0043's terms). Installed machine-level by the owner (aqua:google-antigravity/antigravity-cli), not in mise.toml; check with agy --version. Its self-updater moved it from 1.5.3 to 1.5.5; by agy's own logs it then ran 1.5.6 from 2026-11-12 and 1.5.8 from 2026-11-13, and 1.5.7 never ran here. Whether the updater or the daily agy update (ADR 0065) made those two moves is UNVERIFIED. The pin followed after the release notes were read. 1.5.4 and 1.5.5: Auto mode for agy acp, a swarm preview, fixes; nothing that changes a review-only reader. 1.5.6 to 1.5.8, read 2026-11-13. 1.5.6 loosens Auto mode's review of commands that leave the terminal sandbox: GitHub API reads and single-file downloads skip the checks a clone gets, and reading ~/.ssh/config, known_hosts, authorized_keys or *.pub no longer counts as reading secrets. 1.5.7 makes Auto the default Agent Mode for a session with no saved mode, headless -p runs included, wherever Auto is available, and Default elsewhere; a strict Tool Permission takes precedence over Auto. 1.5.7 also fixes a PreToolUse hook's auto_approve, or a wildcard command(*) allow rule, bypassing an admin-enforced review. 1.5.8 adds Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Carbon for an API-key sign-in, and Hydrogen alone for Application Default Credentials. 1.5.8 fixes a path bypass in the terminal sandbox's network proxy, and permission rules being ignored for MCP tools loaded up front and for the /browser subagent's tools. Orca's launch carries its bypass flag (ADR 0045 rule 2), and whether 1.5.7's Auto default reaches such a launch is UNVERIFIED. Its troubleshooting page documents AGY_CLI_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true, set in the shell profile, to stop the updater; ADR 0065 keeps the updater on (reversing ADR 0045), so the pin is the version last read, and scripts/bootstrap --install removes the line an earlier run wrote to ~/.zshrc. Orca sets the variable in each Antigravity launch that submits a prompt, so its workers do not update; agy update does it at once.

DeepSeek Harness (npm @deepseek-ai/dsh), the engine under dsh-tui, a review-only Orca worker from another model family (ADR 0045, under ADR 0043's terms). Every tag is a pre-release. Machine-level, not in mise.toml (npm:@deepseek-ai/dsh, which at 0.2.2-rc.2 needs Node >=24.9 by its apps/cli/package.json, with pnpm for its profile); check with dsh --version. Landing this pin moves that install: step (d) of the maintenance agent (ADR 0065) sets the global dsh to main's pin at its next round, and the landing lane runs the same step at once inside the install window below. Its release note says to upgrade every process that shares session storage together, and the desktop app runs this version on the same ~/.dsh (the dsh-desktop entry's pin). A move of this pin follows one order (ADR 0045, the 2026-11-13 line under its held bullet): a rehearsal in throwaway homes first; then one install window, opened only while DeepSeek dispatch is held and no dsh-tui session runs, in which the landing, the global move, each worker profile's refresh to home/dsh/profiles.json by exact dsh plugin adds and removes, and scripts/bootstrap --install follow in that order; it closes when scripts/bootstrap --check shows the review patch ok and scripts/dsh-profiles shows each worker profile ok. Until a profile is refreshed, this engine denies at startup the 0.2.1-rc.3 hook packages it carries, so the hook row, and home/dsh/hooks/guard.mjs with it, does not load there, and in dsh-tui it skips dsh-TUI 0.17.0's bundle (rehearsed for dsh-tui on 2026-11-13; app-boot README L56). dsh-v0.2.2-rc.3 (published 2026-11-13T07:56Z) is newer and outside dsh-TUI 0.20.0's peer lists (its package.json), so rc.2 is the newest the TUI admits. The dsh-tui profile records four community plugins and two of the engine's own hook packages (home/dsh/profiles.json), chosen for workflow from a community list that is not a review: aegis 2.15.0 (GanyuanRan/Aegis at commit e5f43c548a06, MIT), dsh-doublecheck 0.9.31 (PerryLink, Apache-2.0), dsh-memento 0.5.30 (PerryLink, Apache-2.0), dsh-tui-find 0.5.2 (xiaoxiaohaigui, MIT), and the hook packages @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code and @deepseek-ai/dsh-hook-protocol 0.2.2-rc.2 (deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, MIT). Aegis v2.15.1 (2026-11-13) is newer than the recorded 2.15.0 and is not taken here: it is its own move. dsh-doublecheck 0.9.31's grill, which dsh-tui runs (grill: true), now reaches the workflow engine a preset mounts, so its report's verification, on by default, can run its forked checks where 0.9.30 skipped them, and a skipped run states why; the change adds no network client, storage path or credential read (GitHub's compare of the two releases, lib/grill/index.js). Four plugins leave the profile with this pin: dsh-advisor, which is inert there (ADR 0086 rule 5); dsh-llm-fallbacks, which hands a failing turn to a second model (npm: "Automatic provider/model fallback chains ... when LLM requests keep failing"), an addition ADR 0072 rule 6 keeps to the build arm; dsh-github-skills, which ADR 0094 rule 5 declines; and dsh-fail-guard, which the profile carried with no record. A scripted rehearsal on 2026-11-13 installed each worker profile exactly as home/dsh/profiles.json records it, with the canon block in dsh-tui, in throwaway DSH_HOMEs with the pinned pnpm, and composed each with --dump-config: every step exit 0, no admission refusal, no duplicate id and no terminal_* tool, and in dsh-tui session-log and memento off, approval never and fs-observation-policy on; nothing was started. Versions are as that install resolved them, licences from npm's metadata and, for aegis, its LICENSE file at that commit. Since the proposed ADR 0086 the machine carries two named configurations beside stock. The review configuration added @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-terminal-bundle to the dsh-tui profile at 0.2.1-rc.3; at this pin it carries no terminal bundle, since the bundle's panel backend needs the Web bundle's terminal controller (ADR 0086 rule 2's 2026-11-13 pointer; that bundle's own entry), so the dsh-tui profile carries the set above with no addition. That removes only the bundle's own terminal tools: a worker's bash is dsh-tool-bash, which the bundle does not provide (the bundle's entry). The build configuration is `dsh --profile headless -`, a one-shot runner carrying aegis, dsh-doublecheck 0.9.30, dsh-memento 0.5.30 at writePolicy auto, dsh-subagent-codex and dsh-subagent-claude-code 0.2.2-rc.2, and the two hook packages at 0.2.2-rc.2 that the worker-parity row in its own patch loads (home/dsh/profiles.json). Neither configuration has an eval run, so both are UNVERIFIED. At this pin the web service's default search is DeepSeek's Search API (searchProvider deepseek-search-api, where 0.2.1-rc.3 composed deepseek-official), which receives each query, a result count and, unless sendOriginalQuestion is off, the latest human prompt cut to 128 characters (dsh-web-deepseek-api's README L27, L44, L75). All four worker profiles compose web search: dsh-tui through the standard preset's own tool-web (packages/bundle/web-app/presets/standard.patch.yml L123-127), the other three through dsh-base's row (the rehearsal's compositions). No row turns sendOriginalQuestion off. That is a recorded limit, not an addition: the recipient is DeepSeek, which already receives every worker turn in full through the chat route (agent-default-model's provider deepseek-official in each composition), so the prefix reaches no new party, and billing follows the conversation's route (README L64); it is stock engine behaviour, so ADR 0072 rule 6 is not engaged (ADR 0086's 2026-11-13 line). The desktop app is its own entry, dsh-desktop, at the version it runs (ADR 0143), and reviews nothing.

Community terminal interface for DeepSeek Harness, the program Orca launches for it (dsh-tui .) under agent id dsh (its CLI bundle); which versions Orca's fixtures used is UNVERIFIED; 0.20.0 names DSH 0.2.2-rc.2 its primary compatibility target, and its peer ranges end at that version (README, package.json; ADR 0045). Machine-level, not in mise.toml (npm:@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui); landing this pin moves that install, by step (d) of the maintenance agent (ADR 0065) at its next round and by the landing lane at once inside the install window (deepseek-harness's entry); its profile lives in the user's home, and its update command aligns the TUI, the dsh engine and the global launcher as one set, outside the pins (DSH_TUI_UPDATE_ENGINE=0 leaves the engine alone). Its README says to upgrade together every process that opens the same session store, since catalogs written by 0.2.2-rc.2 subagents cannot be opened by older DSH. Its profiles send session logs to the configured base URL by default (session-log-deepseek.enabled, true); its configuration page at v0.20.0 documents a user profile patch row that sets it false, which scripts/bootstrap --install adds to the dsh-tui profile with the dsh-memento row memento.enabled false (ADR 0045), with an approval row (policy never) and a permission row whose read-only and workspace-write presets refuse, so a request for wider access is refused instead of asked (ADR 0136), and with an fs-observation-policy row disabled false, which keeps read-before-write on in the dsh-tui profile, where dsh-v0.2.2-rc.2's dsh-base ships it off, once --install has written the block (by the source it also decides the standard preset's file tools; not run, ADR 0045's 2026-11-13 Evidence); headless, review-acp and build-acp run without it (ADR 0136's 2026-11-13 line).

DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds the CI run's allowlisted metadata (provider, repository, refs, commit, workflow, job, run id and URL) as one user message on a turn's first step, read from fixed environment fields; outside CI it does nothing. Its source at the pin makes no network call, writes no file and keeps nothing across sessions, so it may run in the reviewer arm (ADR 0072 rule 6). Installed only into a throwaway DSH_HOME profile, never ~/.dsh or a profile in use (ADR 0072 rule 5). Override of the host's compatibility guard: its peer range for dsh-agent and dsh-llm is ^0.1.0-rc.6, which excludes the pinned dsh 0.2.2-rc.2 as it excluded 0.2.1-rc.3, under which dsh refused the install (judged after the git fetch, then the profile restored) ("Running it may cause crashes or data loss") until the exact-version exemption dsh offers was granted in that profile alone (ADR 0094). An exemption names exact runtime versions (plugin-manager README), so the one granted for 0.2.1-rc.3 does not cover 0.2.2-rc.2. A named configuration, UNVERIFIED until the review and build evals score it; a crash or data loss there retires it.

The Agent Client Protocol, v1: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio between a client and an agent (initialize, session setup, session/prompt with session/update notifications, session/cancel). DeepSeek Harness serves it with `dsh --profile acp` through @deepseek-ai/dsh-acp 0.2.2-rc.2, which says it exposes only the standard ACP v1 surface, leaves out session/load, and builds on @agentclientprotocol/sdk 1.4.0, generated from schema-v1.21.0; the review-acp and build-acp profiles a worker is driven through stand on it (ADR 0095). Tracked by the schema release tags and held to the schema-v1. line, so a schema-v2 release does not move it. The wire version is the integer 1, raised only for a breaking change. Whether dsh conforms is UNVERIFIED: no conformance run exists.

The community index of DeepSeek Harness plugins (10,581 entries at the pin), which lists every plugin ADR 0094 adopts or excludes. A reference, never a source of trust (ADR 0072 rule 3): its own notice says "Being on this list is not a security review" and "Tool approvals don't sandbox plugin code", and its disclaimer that listing "is not an endorsement". Nothing is installed from it: each plugin it names gets its own entry, pin and source read through adopt-upstream (ADR 0094, ADR 0095). It publishes no tags, so it tracks the default branch.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp-app 0.2.2-rc.2, DeepSeek Harness's own profile bundle (packages/bundle/acp-app) that serves the Agent Client Protocol over stdio through @deepseek-ai/dsh-acp, over dsh-base. Its patch sets the coding-agent persona and a default provider deepseek-official and model deepseek-v4-flash, disables the session-title model call, and starts dsh-acp only after its command provider accepts the invocation. Both the review-acp and build-acp profiles carry it (ADR 0095). Its own source has no network, file or subprocess call; what dsh-acp does is the protocol (acp-spec). Shares the deepseek-harness pin and moves with it. Running either profile is UNVERIFIED.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-terminal-bundle 0.2.2-rc.2 (packages/experimental/terminal-bundle), the version last read: six experimental global terminal tools that keep shell processes alive across tool calls, and two read-only tools that list and read the terminals the person opened, in an isolated terminal registry; shipped switched off in Web and Desktop. At 0.2.1-rc.3 review-acp and build-acp carried it, and ADR 0086 chose it as the one addition of its review configuration on the dsh-tui profile. At dsh-v0.2.2-rc.2 it is in no worker profile (ADR 0086 rule 2's 2026-11-13 pointer for dsh-tui, ADR 0095 item 4's for review-acp and build-acp; home/dsh/profiles.json). Its backend is now dsh-terminal-panel, not dsh-terminal-bash, and the panel requires the terminalController service (the inject list in its src/index.ts, L22). Only @deepseek-ai/dsh-api-terminal-controller provides that service, for the Web sidebar's terminals, and its README says the Web bundle mounts it (L28); the web-app bundle is the only one whose cordis.patch.yml composes it. Without it, read in source, the panel stays pending (Cordis's lifecycle tutorial) and the terminal tools fail with NO_BACKEND (packages/terminal/terminal/src/index.ts), so a worker profile would carry tools that fail instead of falling back; no tool was called, so that is UNVERIFIED. Its only tools are the six terminal_* tools of dsh-tool-terminal (its src/index.ts, L166-396) and, new at this pin, the panel's user_terminal_list and user_terminal_read (its src/tools.ts, L87, L116), so leaving it out removes no other tool. No worker's bash comes from it: bash is @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash, whose inject list names none of the bundle's services (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts, L37), and the one service the bundle provides is its terminals registry, which its group isolates (its cordis.patch.yml). dsh-tui takes bash from the standard preset (packages/bundle/web-app/presets/standard.patch.yml, L21-23), which dsh-TUI registers at run time and names as its default (its src/dsh-adapter/bundled-presets.ts and cordis.patch.yml), and review-acp and build-acp take it from dsh-base's own tool-bash row (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml, L281-283; the rehearsal's compositions). The bundle's own code is empty. The entry stays at dsh-v0.2.2-rc.2, and the bundle returns to a profile only through a new adoption.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-codex 0.2.2-rc.2 (packages/subagent/subagent-codex): a subagent_codex tool that runs one self-contained task in a fresh unattended Codex thread in the parent workspace and returns the answer. It bundles its own @openai/codex 0.153.4, outside the codex-cli pin. Native Codex configuration and authentication stay authoritative: key-like variables are scrubbed from the child's environment, so it runs under whatever login CODEX_HOME and HOME point to where dsh started (in an Orca-started session, an Orca-managed home). permissionMode defaults to never, which declines approvals and leaves the sandbox to Codex's settings; the login, mode and sandbox build-acp gets are UNVERIFIED. Another model family answers and it edits the parent workspace, so it is build arm only, by extension of ADR 0072 rule 6 (it sends a task, not the transcript): build-acp carries it and review-acp does not. A result that used it belongs to that family (ADR 0086). Shares the deepseek-harness pin and moves with it.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code 0.2.2-rc.2 (packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code): a subagent_claude_code tool that runs one self-contained task as a fresh unattended Claude Code session in the parent workspace through @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.263 (SEE LICENSE IN README.md, not MIT), which bundles Claude Code 2.1.263, behind the claude-code pin, and never falls back to the host claude. Native Claude settings and authentication stay authoritative: it reads the host's user, project and local settings, and the child gets the profile's env option over the parent environment with key-like and DSH_ variables scrubbed, so it runs under the Claude configuration directory (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.claude) and its Keychain login unless a surviving provider variable or apiKeyHelper outranks it. permissionMode defaults to dontAsk: the host's allow rules and read-only defaults run, the rest is denied. It may read and write the host's auto memory (UNVERIFIED). The login and mode build-acp gets are UNVERIFIED. Another model family answers and it edits the parent workspace, so it is build arm only, by extension of ADR 0072 rule 6 (it sends a task, not the transcript): build-acp carries it and review-acp does not. Shares the deepseek-harness pin and moves with it.

The DeepSeek Harness desktop app (apps/desktop), installed by the owner as a macOS app (com.deepseek.dsh, notarized, Developer ID NAN929V4UM) and updated by its own updater from the vendor's feed, not by mise; check with scripts/dsh-desktop-check. The owner's enhanced tier (ADR 0143): its desktop profile belongs to no Orca arm and is no eval's configuration, and each plugin in it needs an entry at the version it carries; on 2026-11-13 no record listed its 16 packages at those versions. The pin is the version the installed app runs, the version last read, as ADR 0065 rule 3 sets for Antigravity's self-updater: it moves after an app update, through adopt-upstream, and does not move the deepseek-harness pin, which is the CLI engine Orca's workers run. Every tag is a pre-release, and the updater takes pre-releases on either channel.

Package manager dsh-tui needs to build and update its profile (ADR 0045). Installed machine-level by the owner (mise pnpm 10.34.9), not in mise.toml; check with pnpm --version. It runs on node 24.22.2, which this repository's mise.toml requests (node = "24", the node entry); mise ls -g lists no node. Held 2026-11-10: v12.19.0 (published 2026-11-10) is two major versions past v10. The v11.0.0 notes (2026-04-28) require Node 22 or later, turn on strictDepBuilds, blockExoticSubdeps and a one-day minimumReleaseAge by default, replace the build-dependency settings with allowBuilds, and read .npmrc for auth and registry only. Among the v12.0.0 notes (2026-08-26): git dependencies on known hosts resolve through HTTPS, an unrecognised pnpm-workspace.yaml setting fails where the project's pnpm pin is satisfied, --frozen-lockfile false is gone, engineStrict is stricter, and cyclic peer dependencies re-key a lockfile once. dsh-TUI at v0.20.0, as at v0.17.0 and v0.19.0, asks for pnpm 10 or newer (docs/getting-started.en.md: 'CI uses 11'), so the pinned 10.34.9 is inside its range; its package.json pins packageManager pnpm@11.21.0, and its README documents pnpm 11's blocked install scripts, which its update command configures. Its CI runs only pnpm 11 (newest v11 tag v11.28.12, published 2026-11-13), so v12 with dsh-tui is UNVERIFIED. Pin and hand install move together. mise's minimum_release_age (ADR 0008) does not filter an exact version such as pnpm@12.19.0 (mise settings page), so it would not hold a hand install. No record sets a waiting period for a pin moved by hand (ADR 0016's seven days is the bot's; ADR 0001 only quotes Dependabot's default). Re-read 2026-11-11: dsh-tui is its one consumer here (the OmniRoute gateway installs through mise's npm backend, not pnpm). On 2026-11-13, with the dsh pins moving to dsh-v0.2.2-rc.2 and dsh-TUI v0.20.0 (whose package.json still pins packageManager pnpm@11.21.0), a scripted rehearsal installed the four worker profiles (dsh-tui, headless, review-acp and build-acp) as home/dsh/profiles.json records them, each in a throwaway DSH_HOME, through the rc.2 engine's dsh plugin install with the pinned 10.34.9 on node 24.22.2, each exit 0. That shows the install alone: dsh-tui's update command and a build under pnpm 10 were not run, so both are UNVERIFIED. Look again by 2026-12-10, ADR 0045's review-by.

Computes the deflated Sharpe ratio that gates a ranking (ADR 0010, computed per ADR 0031): measures.expected_max_sharpe_ratio, probabilistic_sharpe_ratio and deflated_sharpe_ratio follow Bailey and Lopez de Prado (2014), eqs. 1-2. The gate calls only those three; the test also reads its mean, standard_deviation, skew and kurtosis. Moved 2026-11-10 from v1.12.8: v1.12.9's notes list two prior-model fixes and type-check rules updated for ty 0.0.100; in the files this repository reads, measures/ and population/ are unchanged and portfolio/_base.py, portfolio/_portfolio.py and utils/stats.py change only in ty: ignore comments. A move touches pyproject.toml and uv.lock (uv add skfolio==<version>), src/canon_trading/ranking.py, returns_matrix.py and ledger.py, tests/test_deflated_sharpe.py, docs/architecture.md (the returns-matrix and gate rows) and ADR 0031's version lines; the past reads ADRs 0032, 0035 and 0041 record, and measurements a module header dates to a version, stay as written.

Holds the trial ledger ADR 0010 asks for (ADR 0035): a study in a local SQLite file through RDBStorage, one trial per backtest through ask and tell. A trial is asked for before its run and told FAIL by this repo's code if the run raises; Study.trials returns every state, so N is read back; user attributes hold each trial's config and daily returns.

Carries the dates of the returns matrix (ADR 0010 step 2): skfolio's Portfolio reads observation dates only from a DataFrame, and Population.returns_df joins them. Used to index each trial's series, drop closed days and trim to the common range; no statistic is computed with it.

Read-only SQL over the catalog's Parquet in place and over the run reports: an embedded library, no daemon, no pyarrow (its PyPI metadata puts pyarrow in the 'all' extra only). Opened only through canon_trading.catalog_query, which locks external access to the exact files a query reads. Chosen over Polars by measurement on a catalog snapshot (ADR 0153). The engine is duckdb/duckdb v2.0.0.

Measured against DuckDB as the catalog's read-only query engine and not adopted (ADR 0153): it documents no means by which a write is refused and no footer-only row count, so the coverage grid could not be read without touching row data. Not installed or imported.

OmniRoute (npm omniroute), a local OpenAI-compatible gateway, adopted on the owner's word to start GPT and other non-Anthropic runtimes through one endpoint (ADR 0056). No Anthropic or Claude credential, account or model is configured in it; Claude Code keeps its own login. Installed only on request, from mise's gateway config environment: mise.gateway.toml, locked in mise.gateway.lock with its npm dependency graph under .mise/locks/mise.gateway/ (mise -E gateway install --locked npm:omniroute). No mise field: scripts/canon lint reads mise.toml alone, so scripts/test-lanes holds mise.gateway.toml's version to this pin, and scripts/bootstrap --check compares the installed version with it. Started on demand by mise -E gateway run omniroute:serve with its settings fixed in that task and its storage key read from the login keychain. The repository was renamed from diegosouzapw/OmniRoute; the pin is at or above both fixes for GHSA-hf57-cqmx-p4gr (3.8.49 and 3.8.50).

Agent Orchestrator (AO), a local desktop workspace that runs a daemon and gives each task its own agent, branch and worktree: a host in the same class as Orca (ADR 0018). Not adopted; nothing installed or imported. Its docs say the npm CLI @aoagents/ao is frozen at 0.10.0, though the npm registry lists 0.10.3 as latest; the repository publishes nightly pre-releases several times a day beside stable tags about every two or three days. Permission model and cost tracking are UNVERIFIED (its migration page covers neither).

Gas City, an orchestration-builder SDK for software factories of coding agents, with work held as beads in Dolt: a framework, not a desktop host (ADR 0018). Successor to Gas Town (gastownhall/gastown), which its author's page calls retired (the repository still receives commits). Not adopted; nothing installed or imported. Its v1.5.1 notes (24 Oct 2026) mention a fix to Claude permission prompts and cost estimates for the Claude 5 family; its release notes also name Claude's builtin permission_mode "unrestricted" as a default; its permission model is otherwise UNVERIFIED.

upstreams.why: Ships SPA (White's reality check as refined by Hansen) and StepM (Romano and Wolf) with a stationary bootstrap: tests of each registered arm's mean outcome against a base arm's with the number of arms counted. They compare mean loss differentials, not Sharpe ratios, so the Sharpe-against-Sharpe test ADR 0010 leaves out of scope stays out. Adopted for one consumer, canon_trading.arm_comparison, a diagnostic report beside the gate that calls arch.bootstrap.SPA and StepM on a daily return matrix, one row per session day (ADR 0104); nothing else imports arch, and no producer of that matrix from the replay is built yet. Pinned to 9.0.0 and no earlier: its notes say the default studentize=True had no effect in SPA and StepM before it. MCS, the volatility models and the unit-root tests are not used. The gate is unchanged. A move touches pyproject.toml and uv.lock (uv add arch==<version>), ADR 0104's version lines, and canon_trading.arm_comparison with its test: the module refuses any version but the one it names, and its header cites the pinned source by line.

Draws NautilusTrader's tearsheet: nautilus_trader.analysis.tearsheet imports plotly and raises ImportError without it, and its create_tearsheet writes one self-contained HTML file from a BacktestResult (ADR 0109). Declared directly at 7.1.0, the version uv.lock already held through skfolio and inside the 7.x range of NautilusTrader's visualization extra, so that code here does not rest on another package's dependency. One consumer, the replay tearsheet, one HTML file per symbol replay in a folder git ignores, which is not built yet; this repository draws no figure of its own. Kaleido, which the extra also lists and only a static image needs, is not adopted. A move touches pyproject.toml and uv.lock (uv add plotly==<version>) and must stay inside the range the pinned NautilusTrader and skfolio accept.

Reads SEC EDGAR filings (current filings, a company's submissions, 8-K items) and waits at 9 requests a second by default, under the 10 a second the SEC states; the limiter is per process, so one process at a time uses it. Adopted for one consumer, a GET-only filings recorder for the names the ranking lists, with its records outside the repository (ADR 0108); the recorder is not built yet. Installed in a project of its own, filings/, with its own uv.lock and environment, and never in the shared one: it requires pyarrow, and with pyarrow installed pandas backs its text columns with Arrow, which changes the environment the gate and the studies run in. The identity the SEC asks a client to declare is entered locally by the owner in a setting git does not track; the recorder passes it to set_identity() before any request, on every request path, and refuses to start with none, because at the pin a request with EDGAR_IDENTITY unset can reach a terminal prompt. The value is never written to a tracked file, a log or a record. Pinned to 6.0.0, not 5.62.1: until 6.0 set_identity() wrote the identity to the INFO log. edgar.ai is never imported (its install_skill() writes into ~/.claude/skills) and the two console scripts the install adds, edgartools and edgartools-mcp, are never run: neither a skill nor an MCP server from it is an adopted extension (ADR 0004). A filing is a label and changes no order. A move is uv add edgartools==<version> run from filings/, with this entry, ADR 0108's title and the row in docs/architecture.md; filings/tests/test_upstream_contract.py holds those and the installed version to one, since the lint's pypi comparison reads the root's uv.lock only.
